articles.title: In 2020, Minnesota funded a $1.918 million Shell Rock River habitat program; by 2025, it had protected or restored 588 acres
articles.summary: US News: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report.
articles.body: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report from the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, the program ultimately protected, restored or enhanced 588 acres of habitat in the Shell Rock River watershed, exceeding its original goal of 483 acres.A habitat program takes shapeThe funding was provided under Minnesota Laws 2020, with the appropriation directed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an agreement with the Shell Rock River Watershed District. The funding was intended to support land acquisition as well as the restoration and enhancement of aquatic habitat within the watershed. The program focused on several types of conservation work, including acquiring properties, restoring wetlands and improving aquatic habitat. The projects were selected using conservation planning and monitoring intended to identify areas where habitat improvements could provide significant benefits.The Shell Rock River Watershed is a shallow-lake system that supports fish, waterfowl and other wildlife. According to the final report, restoration projects were targeted at addressing habitat degradation and improving conditions for native fish, waterfowl and wildlife.Three properties protectedOne part of Phase IX involved acquiring three properties: the Glenville Property, the Bancroft Property, and the Church Lake Property. The District closed on the Glenville Property in March 2021 and the Bancroft Property in September 2021. For the Church Lake Property, the District transferred the deed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources in December 2024 after acquiring and restoring the parcel.The final report says these acquisitions contributed to the program's permanent protection of 218 acres. Another 370 acres of habitat and wetlands were enhanced or restored through the program. Together, those accomplishments contributed to the reported total of 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.Wetlands and prairie restoredThe program included several restoration projects beyond property acquisition. The Bancroft Wetland Restoration was initiated in 2020, with construction beginning in June 2024 and largely completed by the fall of that year. Additional seeding work was completed in spring 2025. Another project focused on Panicum Prairie, where habitat enhancement work was carried out across 300 acres. The project involved native prairie vegetation and was substantially completed in February 2025, with final work completed in May.The program also supported the Fountain Lake In-Lake Habitat Project. Work included additional rock reefs and rock boulder clusters intended to improve fish habitat. The report notes that Phase IX funds were used to expand the scope of this work after the District determined additional funds were available. These projects addressed different parts of the watershed's ecosystem, from wetlands and prairie habitat to aquatic areas. The broader aim was to improve habitat conditions while protecting areas that could provide long-term benefits for wildlife.More acres than plannedThe program's original accomplishment plan called for 483 acres. By the end of the project, the final total had reached 588 acres, 105 acres more than initially planned. The report attributes the increase to the addition of the In-Lake Habitat Project and the Church Lake Property to Phase IX.According to the report, all grant funds were spent. The final grant expenditure remained $1.918 million, while the program's final total including leverage was $1.9479 million.A longer-term conservation effortThe work is intended to continue beyond the end of the grant. The Shell Rock River Watershed District relies on multiple funding sources, including a local option sales tax, local levy and public funding, to maintain conservation projects. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources will also maintain the Church Lake Property, which it owns.The program's results illustrate how a single state-funded conservation effort can combine land protection, wetland restoration, prairie enhancement and aquatic habitat improvements. Rather than focusing on one habitat type, Phase IX combined several projects across the Shell Rock River watershed. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored. The completed work represents a combination of permanent land protection and habitat improvements designed to support Minnesota's fish, waterfowl and wildlife over the long term.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
articles.summary: US News: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential .
articles.body: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Who is Dan Scavino?Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications. During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Who is Natalie Harp?Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Who is Walt Nauta?Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Quote of the day by King Charles: "To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dearâ¦" - a tribute to Queen Elizabeth, on gratitude, service and a son's farewell
articles.summary: UK News: Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son.
articles.body: Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son, King Charles III, addressed the nation the following day, speaking as both a new monarch and a grieving son at the same time. Recorded in the Blue Drawing Room at Buckingham Palace, with a framed portrait of his mother resting on the desk beside him, his tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service. It became one of the most widely remembered moments of that entire period, quoted on front pages across the country the following morning. For millions watching, the address offered a rare glimpse behind the crown, where duty and private grief briefly occupied space. His carefully chosen words also captured the enormous responsibility that had suddenly passed to him, making the moment deeply personal and historically significant. The speech also reassured a grieving public that the values associated with Elizabethâs reign would continue, while Charles acknowledged the changes that lay ahead. His measured tone reflected both continuity and transition as Britain entered a new chapter.The address also marked the beginning of a new constitutional era, as Charles formally assumed the role his mother had held for seven decades. His message balanced continuity with change, reassuring the public while acknowledging the profound personal loss.Quote of the day by King Charles"To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late Papa, I want simply to say this: Thank you. Thank you for your love and devotion to our family and to the family of nations you have served so diligently all these years. May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest"What is the meaning of King Charles' quoteAt its heart, the message is about gratitude, love and farewell. Charles begins by describing his mother's death as a "last great journey," a gentle way of naming the end of a life, before referring directly to her reunion with her late husband, Prince Philip, who had died in April 2021. Rather than dwelling on the enormous constitutional change actually taking place, Charles places his mother's role firmly within a family context first. He thanks her for the love and devotion she gave to her family, before widening that same gratitude to the people and nations she served. The simplicity of the words "thank you," repeated before he expands on what he is actually grateful for, turns the tribute into an expression of appreciation for an entire lifetime of service.Why King Charles thanked Queen Elizabeth IIQueen Elizabeth II became monarch in 1952 and remained on the throne for more than seven decades, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history. Across that period, she served under fifteen British prime ministers and witnessed enormous political, social and technological change. For Charles, though, her significance was never limited to her constitutional role alone. She was also, simply, his mother. His tribute moves between these two identities throughout, recognising her commitment to the "family of nations" she served while speaking about her in the deeply personal language of a son saying goodbye to his parent.The personal meaning behind "my darling Mama"The phrase "my darling Mama" gave the speech a genuinely intimate quality that stood apart from the formal language normally associated with royal addresses. Charles was speaking to a global audience, and yet the words themselves were directed towards one single person. Calling his mother "Mama" reflected the private family relationship sitting behind the public institution. Elizabeth II had been Queen to millions of people, but to her son she remained, simply, his mother. That contrast is really what gave the tribute its personal weight rather than letting it feel purely ceremonial.What "the family of nations" actually meansCharles' reference to the "family of nations" reflects Queen Elizabeth II's role across the Commonwealth, a voluntary association of independent countries, many with historical connections to the British Empire, of which she served as Head throughout her entire reign. Her role involved maintaining relationships with leaders and people across every member country, while representing a genuine continuity through decades of political change. Describing these countries as a "family of nations" highlighted exactly the relationships his mother had worked to maintain across the whole of her reign.Why Charles' farewell centred on serviceA central theme running through Queen Elizabeth II's public life was duty. In her 1952 accession broadcast, she pledged her life to the service of the people of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. Seven decades later, Charles' farewell returned directly to that same idea. Describing her as having served "so diligently all these years" recognised both the length and the sheer consistency of that commitment. It also reflected the unusual nature of her reign specifically, since she continued carrying out official duties well into her nineties, including appointing Liz Truss as prime minister only two days before her death.The Shakespeare reference at the end of the speechCharles closed his tribute with the words "May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The line comes from William Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 5, Scene 2, spoken by Horatio as he mourns his friend at the play's close, "Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The reference gave Charles' speech a genuinely literary and solemn conclusion, connecting his personal farewell to one of the most recognisable expressions of grief in English literature, and its suggestion of a peaceful passage into rest made it particularly fitting for a speech delivered the day after losing a parent.How the quote reflects the relationship between duty and familyOne of the most powerful aspects of Charles' tribute is how it brings together two sides of Queen Elizabeth II's life at once, a mother within her own family, and a monarch with responsibilities reaching far beyond it. Charles' words acknowledge both directly, first thanking her for her "love and devotion to our family," then expanding that same gratitude outward to the people and nations she served. In the same speech, he also announced that Prince William and Catherine would become the new Prince and Princess of Wales, and expressed his love for Harry and Meghan "as they continue to build their lives overseas," a reminder that even a historic constitutional address remained, underneath it, a message about family.How to apply the message in daily lifeThe circumstances behind this quote are genuinely unique, but its central message of gratitude applies just as well to ordinary relationships. Say thank you while you still can, since the people who matter most should never have to wait for a farewell to hear how much they are actually appreciated. Recognise quiet, unglamorous forms of service, since care and responsibility are often given without much recognition at all. Value family relationships alongside professional achievement, and remember that simple words of love and appreciation tend to become more meaningful, not less, with time.Some other memorable quotes by King Charles"I am a dangerous person because I mind about things.""It is important to be able to stand back and see the bigger picture.""The environment is something that is very close to my heart.""I think we have to be very careful about what we do to the natural world."Why King Charles' farewell remains memorableCharles' first address as King carried an unavoidable constitutional significance, and yet its most memorable passage was deeply personal. He was not simply acknowledging the end of a historic reign. He was saying goodbye to the woman who had been his mother for more than seven decades. The repeated "thank you" captures the central emotion of the entire tribute. After a lifetime defined by public duty, Charles chose to close his first address as monarch with something considerably more private, a reminder that behind every title and institution sits an ordinary human relationship. A queen can be a constitutional figure to an entire nation while remaining, simply, "Mama" to her own son.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person withâ¦" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
articles.summary: US News: Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a ser.
articles.body: Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox, the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"Where this quote actually comes fromThis line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem. It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretchesLife inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.How humour actually helps people manage stressStress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.Why laughing at your own mistakes actually mattersOne of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationshipsShared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversityFox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problemThere is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Why being naturally serious is not actually a flawFox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered.""I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection.""Family is not an important thing. It's everything.""Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."Why people still find meaning in this quoteHumour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: UK News: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structur.
articles.body: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Who is Gautam Rangarajan?Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.Burnham's government overhaulThe appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Fired Texas judge speaks out as dirty water firestorm engulfs town
articles.summary: Jennifer Combs' Facebook post about Trinidad water led to her felony arrest, a fired judge, and a Texas Rangers investigation now rocking the city.
articles.body: When we first introduced you to Jennifer Combs, the facts already sounded hard to believe. The Texas mom said police arrested her after she used Facebook to collect complaints about discolored water in Trinidad. Combs spent 23 hours in jail on a felony false alarm or report charge. A Henderson County grand jury later declined to indict her. She has since filed a federal lawsuit alleging political retaliation. You can read our original article on Jennifer Combs and the Trinidad, Texas, water controversy. Her arrest, however, did not end the controversy. Police later arrested a man who protested outside Trinidad City Hall. The judge who dismissed his charge says city officials fired her one week later. TEXAS MOM JAILED OVER DIRTY WATER FACEBOOK POST New! Free live CyberGuy class: Protect your money from today's biggest threats Join us Saturday, Aug. 29, at 10 a.m. ET for a free CyberGuy LIVE class covering five simple steps to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward. Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com. Judge Bivens describes what happened inside her courtroom Former Trinidad Municipal Judge Shellena Bivens joined me on "The CyberGuy Report" podcast at CyberGuy.com to explain why she dismissed the protest case and what happened after that decision. Bivens had served as a judge for 16 years. She described herself in a way that was direct and deeply personal. "I've been a damn good judge," Bivens said. "I've tried to be human." The case involved Winston Noles, a citizen journalist known online as Otto the Watchdog. He went to Trinidad after learning about Combs' arrest. Noles stood outside city hall with a sign that used an expletive to criticize "bad cops." Trinidad police arrested him and charged him with misdemeanor disorderly conduct. The department's case centered on a claim that his sign had offended the city's water clerk. Bivens said the evidence presented to her did not support that charge. Judge Bivens says she repeatedly told police to release him Bivens recalled an officer entering her courtroom and presenting two possible outcomes. Police could take Noles to jail or bring him before her for arraignment. Her response was clear.  "You need to let him go," Bivens said. "I said that multiple times. You need to let him go." Bivens dismissed the disorderly conduct charge. She said Noles had not committed a crime by displaying the sign. Local reporting also found that the former water clerk, Colby Reyes, said in writing that Noles had not offended her. Reyes later joined another former city employee in a wrongful termination lawsuit against Trinidad. The lawsuit alleges that city officials fired Reyes because she "refused to lie" about her reaction to the protest. Those allegations have not been proven in court. During our interview, Combs described the situation.  "She would not sign a statement that said she was offended," Combs said. Then came the part that still seems unbelievable. "The judge dropped it. They fired the judge," Combs said. CARIBBEAN HOT SPOT GRIPPED BY WATER CRISIS, AND TOURISTS SCRAMBLE TO RESCHEDULE PLANS Trinidad City Council voted to dismiss Bivens The Trinidad City Council voted 3-1 to dismiss Bivens during a May 28 meeting. Her attorney argued that the council's action was unlawful. The city proceeded with the dismissal. Bivens told me she returned to work and discovered she could no longer enter her office.  "They changed my code when I came in to work on Tuesday," she said. "My security code was changed." She said city leaders ended her 16-year judicial career without giving her a valid reason. When I asked whether she expected a Facebook post about water to cause this much upheaval, she answered quickly.  "Absolutely not. No," Bivens said. "This has been such a crazy journey." Bivens has said publicly that she believes the city retaliated against her because she dismissed Noles' charge. Her attorneys have considered legal action. The city has not admitted that retaliation motivated its vote. CyberGuy sent a request for comment to the mayor and city council through the city’s published contact information but did not hear back before our deadline. Bivens makes an allegation about the former police chief During our interview, Bivens also described an alleged conversation with Charles Gregory, who served as Trinidad's police chief when police arrested Combs. According to Bivens, Gregory entered her office after Combs published her Facebook post.  "I know who it is, and I'm, I'm F---ing getting her. I'm getting her," Bivens recalled him saying. That is Bivens' account of the conversation. CyberGuy has not independently verified that Gregory made the statement. Gregory previously defended the department's decision to pursue Combs. He said her Facebook post created "fear, panic, or unnecessary emergency response within a community." He later resigned, with June 19 reported as his final day. We reached out to the Trinidad Police Department for comment about Bivens' allegations and the department's handling of the arrests. We did not hear back before our deadline. In our earlier CyberGuy report, an attorney representing Trinidad said the city could not discuss details because of active lawsuits.  "The claims against the City of Trinidad will be answered where they belong, in a court of law," attorney Zachary Smith wrote. Another judge questioned the information police provided The warrant process later faced scrutiny from another judge. Henderson County District Judge R. Scott McKee approved the warrant connected to Combs' arrest. He later sent Gregory a letter questioning information that two Trinidad officers had presented. McKee questioned the "accuracy, completeness, and reliability" of the officers' information. According to the letter, the officers failed to disclose citizen complaints and water-quality concerns. They also left out information that could explain the basis for Combs' Facebook post. McKee ordered the two officers to appear before him in person when seeking future warrants. They had previously been allowed to submit requests electronically. That development is important. A judge can only evaluate probable cause using the information police provide. Missing context may change how a judge views the entire case. State investigators documented Trinidad water violations State investigators confirmed that Trinidad's water system had real problems. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality released findings from two investigations on July 1. The first investigation found that Trinidad's system failed to meet state minimums involving total chlorine and iron. The report said the system had returned to compliance by April 22 after a boil water notice. A second investigation began May 15. It resulted in four violations. Investigators documented problems with required chloramine-effectiveness sampling. They also found maintenance issues at the surface water treatment plant. In one sample, investigators recorded 20 color units. The EPA and TCEQ recommend a maximum of 15 color units. These findings do not confirm every medical claim posted online. However, they show that residents were raising concerns about a system with documented deficiencies. Family says teenager suffered burns after showering Combs and Bivens also discussed a Trinidad family that said its 16-year-old daughter developed a serious skin reaction after showering. Medical records obtained by a local TV station described the condition as "most likely chemical burn/severe dermatitis from water she was exposed to." However, the report also stated that it remained unclear whether Trinidad's water treatment process caused the reaction. The family was considering legal action at the time of the report. Bivens told me she knew the family and had seen photographs of the teenager's injuries.  ]"I've seen the pictures," Bivens said. "I know the family of the young girl that got burned." The family's allegation and the medical assessment deserve attention. Still, a final legal or regulatory determination about the cause has not been made. Texas Rangers investigate Trinidad as City Hall staff resigns On July 10, the Texas Rangers confirmed they had opened an investigation involving Trinidad.  "We can confirm the Texas Rangers are investigating," the agency told Dallas affiliate FOX 4. Because the investigation remains active, the Rangers did not disclose its scope. Then, on July 16, all three members of Trinidad's city hall staff resigned. The departing officials were City Manager Cynthia Dosier, City Clerk Sandra Rojas and Municipal Judge Susan Carver. Carver had taken over the municipal judge position after Bivens' dismissal. Mayor Dennis Haws warned that the resignations would create operational problems while the city worked through the transition. The resignations do not prove wrongdoing. They do show how far this controversy has spread since Combs published her original Facebook post. Facebook's role in the Trinidad water fight Combs says people associated with a small group in Trinidad mass reported her Facebook post. The platform then removed it. During our interview, Bivens directed a message at Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.  "Stop trampling on people's rights," Bivens said. "Stop trampling on free speech."  We reached out to Meta for comment on Bivens' message, but did not hear back before our deadline. Facebook's content-moderation system did not arrest Combs. Still, removing a post can erase evidence of what someone said and how other people responded. That is why screenshots matter. Save the original post and relevant comments when documenting a public concern. Keep copies of notices or messages you receive from officials. You should also separate confirmed facts from reports that still need verification. Phrases such as "residents reported" or "we are asking the state to investigate" make that distinction clear. For more ways to control what social platforms collect and preserve your account security, see our five simple tech tips to take back control of social media. Kurt's key takeaways Jennifer Combs says she used Facebook to gather water complaints from people who felt ignored. Police responded with a felony charge, yet a grand jury declined to indict her. Winston Noles then protested her treatment. Judge Shellena Bivens dismissed his disorderly conduct charge because she said the evidence did not support it. Trinidad's City Council fired her one week later.  Since then, another judge has questioned the police warrant process. State investigators have documented water-system violations. The Texas Rangers are also investigating, although they have not revealed the scope. Public officials have every right to correct false information. They also have a duty to respect lawful criticism. Arresting people who question local government creates a chilling effect that can reach far beyond one small town. For more on how this controversy unfolded, check out the full conversation with Judge Bivens on The CyberGuy Report podcast at CyberGuy.com. When a Facebook post about dirty water can lead to two arrests, a fired judge and a Texas Rangers investigation, how safe would you feel speaking up in your own community? They decided to stop for the night after a long session.While Speed was away, Jamal took control of the stream for a short time. He opened the âSelect Worldâ menu and clicked on the first saved world, which was named â???.â He then deleted it. Realizing what he had done, Jamal immediately reacted, saying, âWait! Did I just delete theirâ¦ No!âThat was enough to make the chat fill with âLs,â as viewers thought the duo had lost their progress. The current save had more than 20 hours of work behind it.Speed later woke up and saw messages telling him Jamal had deleted the world. Once he reached his setup, he watched the clip and checked the name of the active save. His reaction made the situation clear.âHe didnât delete ours. Chat, he didnât delete ours. Bro, he was close. Nah, ours is [named âi got a bad b boatâ]â¦ Oh my god, I got scared for a minute.âSo, the viral clip shows Jamal deleting a world, but not the one being used for the current Hardcore run. articles.title: 5 Missing Persons Cases being Investigated in Scott County, Missouri: Dateline
articles.summary: Scott County, Missouri, investigators examine five missing persons cases in the area: Those of Timarius Wiley, Shyann Morrison, David Todd, Pamela Dalton, and Cheryl Scherer.
articles.body: According to the National Crime Information Center, roughly half a million people are reported missing every year in the U.S. While many of those cases are resolved quickly, tens of thousands remain active — and unsolved — for decades. Last year, nearly 10,000 people were reported missing in Missouri. By year’s end, just over 100 were still missing. Scott County, in southeastern Missouri, has a population of about 40,000 people. It has five active missing persons cases. These are their stories. Timarius Wiley Nineteen-year-old Timarius Wiley was last seen on April 17 in Sikeston. He has brown eyes, stands 5 feet, 9 inches tall and weighs about 120 pounds. Sikeston Public Safety Investigator Matt Cotner told “Dateline” he spoke with the detective on the case, who said Timarius reportedly has “been seen and has been in the homes of family members in Charleston, MO.” However, authorities have not been able to confirm that, and the case is still open. Cotner encourages anyone with information about Timarius Wiley’s whereabouts to contact the Public Safety Department at 573-471-6200. ​Shyann Morrison Shyann Morrison ​was last seen at Quick Chek II, a gas station in Sikeston, on Feb. 6, 2021. Shyann, then ​21, was last seen wearing a red fur-trimmed jacket, black pants and brown boots. It is believed she may have been on her way to Texas. Cotner is also working on Shyann’s case. “The biggest challenge is, like with any missing person case, there’s so much unknown,” he told “Dateline.” Cotner said investigators have conducted many interviews with persons of interest. They have also used computer voice stress analysis tests, which measure involuntary stress in the voice, as well as cellphone tower data obtained through search warrants, triangulation techniques and cadaver dogs. Despite those efforts, Cotner said, piecing together what happened to Shyann has been difficult. Over time, information gathered through interviews, search warrants and tips from people connected to the case has helped narrow the focus. “Some people that are in the circle of the people we suspect to be involved have led us to some, um, good tips,” he said. “One of the people that we’re looking at as either being involved or knowing exactly what happened, that person — after a long time of not being able to find that person and denying any knowledge — eventually kind of broke down and gave us, you know, kind of a good explanation of events,” Cotner said. He said information obtained through search warrants also helped investigators identify potential suspects. “We got a very, very good idea of, you know, who we’re kinda looking for,” he said. “We just haven’t been able to make that leap yet.” He added that investigators have been able to weed out misinformation and gain clarity despite what he described as the “lies and the misdirections that we were being told as cover-ups.” Shyann is 5 feet, 7 inches tall and weighs 120 pounds.​ She would be 26 years old today. If anyone has information about Shyann Morrison’s whereabouts, please contact the Sikeston Public Safety Department at 573-471-6200. David Todd David Todd was last seen by his mother at his Scott City residence on Dec. 22, 2020. According to Scott County Sheriff Derick Wheetley, the truck driver, then 55, was last seen by his employer the next day. On Dec. 28, David’s mother reported him missing. Wheetley told “Dateline” that on Dec. 23, there was a car crash near Highway 61 and Azalea Street in Scott County. The vehicle crossed the center line, ran off the right side of the roadway and struck a tree. Wheetley provided the incident report, which says David Todd’s employer had lent him a white Ford F-150, which matched the description of the vehicle towed from the scene of the accident. Wheetley said authorities can’t confirm David was driving the vehicle at the time, but the report says he lives roughly a mile from the crash site. “He was never found by that vehicle or in that vehicle,” Wheetley said. “He hasn’t been seen since that accident.” According to the incident report, David’s mother told detectives that her son had been involved in a car accident about a decade before and that he suffered “from memory loss and at times, a limited mental capacity.” David has blue eyes, is 5 feet, 8 inches tall and weighs about 170 pounds. He has two tattoos on his back, near his shoulder blades. He would be 60 years old today. Anyone with information about David Todd’s whereabouts is urged to contact the Scott City Police Department at 573-264-2121, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Missing Persons Clearinghouse at 866-362-6422 or the Scott County Sheriff’s Office at 573-545-3525.​ Pamela Dalton Pamela Dalton went missing on May 1, 1991. She was 33 years old. Cotner, of the Sikeston Department of Public Safety, said Pamela was last seen in St. Louis, not Sikeston. He told “Dateline” that while the Department of Public Safety has assisted in Pamela’s case, the Scott County Sheriff’s Office is the lead investigating agency. Scott County Detective Sgt. Michael Williams said investigators don’t have a specific address for where Pamela was last seen in St. Louis. Because of that and other jurisdictional issues, Williams said, the case ultimately came to be handled by authorities in Scott County, where Pamela is from. Williams said that investigators have pursued a few leads over the years but that none of them has panned out. He told “Dateline” he has worked on Pamela’s case from the beginning and said there has been speculation that she could have been a victim of Gary Muehlberg, known as the “Package Killer,” who killed women in the St. Louis area in the early 1990s. However, Williams said, there has been no official confirmation linking Pamela’s 1991 disappearance to Muehlberg. In 2022, Muehlberg, who was already serving a life sentence for murder, was linked through DNA evidence to the killings of four women: Robyn Mihan, Brenda Pruitt, Donna Reitmeyer and Sandra Little. He later pleaded guilty to those killings and is serving multiple life sentences without the possibility of parole at the Potosi Correctional Center in Missouri. Williams hopes that somebody out there remembers something that could help investigators determine what happened to Pamela. “​You know, she’s still missing, but she may be a victim in the serial case,” he said. “We need all [the] help and leads.” If anyone has information about Pamela Dalton’s whereabouts, please contact the Sikeston Department of Public Safety at 573-471-4711 or the Scott County Sheriff’s Office at 573-545-3525. Cheryl Scherer It has been more than 47 years since Cheryl Scherer, then 19, vanished from her job at the Rhodes Pump-Ur-Own gas station on April 17, 1979, in Scott City. Authorities believe she was abducted just before noon. Cheryl’s case is the oldest unsolved missing person case in Scott County. “Dateline” spoke with the Scott County Sheriff’s Office and Cheryl’s siblings about her disappearance in Season 5 of the “Dateline: Missing in America” podcast. Sister Diane Scherer-Morris told “Dateline” the family doesn’t believe Cheryl left the gas station on her own. “Never did it cross our minds,” she said. “She’s just not that kind of person. She just would not have done that.” Wheetley became the Scott County sheriff last year. He said he was familiar with Cheryl’s case. ​“It’s a case that’s been talked about a lot,” he told “Dateline.” “All the possibilities of theories and conspiracies have been talked about over time.” Williams, the detective sergeant, joined the case in 2021. Looking back at the initial investigation, Williams said, investigators “did everything that they could in that time period.” More than $400 was missing from the bank bag at the gas station. In recent years, authorities have used DNA testing in the hope of developing new leads. Williams said the testing identified as many as 30 possible DNA profiles on the bag. Investigators are still hopeful the DNA evidence could lead them in the right direction. The sheriff’s office conducted a large-scale excavation for Cheryl this year after eight cadaver dogs alerted to the possible presence of human remains in the same location. They didn’t find Cheryl, but investigators are determined to continue the search. “I use a lot of four-letter words, but ‘quit’ and ‘stop’ is not one of them,” Williams said. In the nearly half-century since Cheryl disappeared, her family has dedicated itself to bringing attention not only to Cheryl’s case, but also to the cases of other missing persons in the area. “Every missing person has a name, and they have a story. And everyone should be able to finish that story,” Diane said. When she disappeared, Cheryl Scherer was 5 feet, 1 inch tall and weighed 100 pounds, with blue eyes and shoulder-length red hair. She would be 67 years old this month. If you have any information about her case, please contact the Scott County Sheriff’s Office at 573-545-3525. If you have a story to share with “Dateline,” please submit it here.

articles.title: Why Japanese firms are being so slow to use AI
articles.summary: Japanese risk aversion and conservatism blamed for slow AI take-up by the country's business sector.
articles.body:
Facing acute labour shortages, ageing demographics and chronic productivity problems, Japanese companies should be fertile ground for the take-up of artificial intelligence (AI). Yet, compared with the US and UK, adoption in many workplaces remains sluggish and cautious.

Japan's response to AI is beginning to resemble one of the country's slow-moving, traditional Noh plays.

All the masked characters up on stage agree that action is urgent, and the call is repeated with solemn agreement. Yet the actors remain frozen in place.

Great for heightening drama, terrible for addressing the country's immediate difficulties.

Data showing the use of AI in the workplace suggests that Japan has fallen behind. Just 8.4% of Japanese workers use AI as part of their job, according to a report , external at the end of last year by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

By contrast, separate statistics puts the US figure at 50%, , external and the UK at 32%. , external In Singapore, which is said to have seen the second-highest , external take up of AI after the United Arab Emirates, and the most in Asia, 56% of workers are said to use AI "multiple times a week". , external

US and Japan take action to prop up yen in rare joint move Published 3 August

US and Japan take action to prop up yen in rare joint move

AI used new levels of 'autonomy and deception' to trick people in safety test Published 5 August

AI used new levels of 'autonomy and deception' to trick people in safety test

So why is Japan dragging its feet? Austin Xu, co-founder of US start-up Kuse AI, says it is due to Japanese companies being conservative and risk adverse. His business recently set up an office in Japan to sell its AI systems to firms in the country.

"There are organisations where process and consensus culture genuinely slow things down," he says. "Where tolerance for AI mistakes is close to zero, especially in anything client facing. Some would rather leave a role unfilled than let a machine handle it."

Xu says the situation in the US is very different, with some businesses already allowing AI agents far more freedom to boost productivity. "In the US, AI colleagues enter as helpers and gradually become part of the workflow. The attitude [of US bosses] is often - let it try, then correct it."

He adds that Japanese companies need more proof before they trust AI enough to use it.

Parrisa Haghirian, professor of international management at the Kyoto University of Advanced Science, agrees that many Japanese companies are too risk adverse to look at AI.

"The challenges of adopting it are the same as adopting any change in Japanese firms. This is why AI use is still quite limited and cautious, especially in the workplace."

Haghirian also contrasts this with the more entrepreneurial culture of the US, arguing that Japanese firms are highly sensitive to error, uncertainty and reputational risk.

"Since generative AI is still not fully reliable, it is mainly used [in Japan] for low-risk tasks such as writing, summarising, or information gathering, but much less for core operations or decision-making and for improving overall processes," she says.

Japan's healthcare sector is said to be particularly slow to look at AI, with some hospitals yet to even fully digitalise patient files. "Paper documents accumulate at a staggering scale," says one employee at a Japanese hospital, who asked not to be named. "It's like the Stone Age."

The Japanese government is aware of the wider problem of low AI adoption, and is trying to get more companies to take up the technology. Last year its AI Promotion Act was passed , external by the country's parliament.

This aims to use light-touch regulation to encourage businesses to invest more in AI. Tokyo pledges that Japan will become "the world's most-friendly country for developing and utilizing AI".

The government believes that the increased use of AI can help Japan improve its productivity. Currently it continues to have the worst level , external in the G7 group of advanced nations.

Japan's Ministry of Finance says that AI adoption by businesses has already increased substantially, , external with 75% of companies now using the technology, up from 11% five years ago.

However, critics argue that at each of these businesses only a tiny proportion of staff are actually using the AI, and that those who do so are only using it to a very limited extent.

Prof Yasushi Ogasawara, an expert on Japan's social system and technology at Meiji University, says there aren't enough tech-savvy people in the workforce.

"Although the Japanese like playing with gadgets such as smartphones, digital literacy is low here," he says.

This is highlighted by one report earlier this year which said Japan faced a shortfall , external of almost 800,000 IT professionals by 2030.

Many companies are also said to struggle with out-of-date computer systems, with around 60% more than 20-years-old.

Moreover, Ogasawara adds that Japanese companies are under more pressure to avoid fuelling unemployment than they are to develop AI which could result in job losses.

"The government is talking about AI, re-skilling, digital skills, but in reality, it is difficult to adapt human resources to digital skills because the top priority is to maintain full employment," he says.

But there is a shift in recruitment, with some companies now prioritising "AI literacy" in their new graduate hiring.

In the private sector, larger firms such as Kanematsu, a major general trading company, are hiring savvy graduates such as Uta Yamaguchi who joined in April.

"I use AI quite often at work," she says. "Many of my colleagues use it a lot. For writing emails for my boss, summarising complicated documents, meeting recording and summarising."

But, by contrast with the US, she says AI systems that can autonomously handle multi-step work are still virtually unheard of in Japan.

However, her employer, known for its forward thinking, now has them onboard.

Ogasawara says that "change in Japan is limited". He adds: "Japanese society expects painless reform, so I think it can be said that drastic reform is difficult, to say the least."

Disruption may be a dirty word in Japan, but without it the productivity gains the country needs could remain elusive.

articles.title: Ayra Starr on her secret relationship and teasing Stevie Wonder
articles.summary: The musician shares the personal stories behind her third album, and the time she teased a legend.
articles.body:
There's resilience, and then there's Ayra Starr.

Two weeks before the release of her new album, Starrgirl, the Nigerian singer posted a photo from hospital, after undergoing "major surgery".

"I was hoping it would be a quick recovery, but it was more complicated than they expected," she told fans , without disclosing the nature of the procedure.

Within seven days, she was back in the dance studio, rehearsing for forthcoming performances with a large bandage strapped across her stomach. TV appearances, fan events and live performances followed.

"I'm healing," she told the US breakfast TV show, Today. "I have strength today. I'm so happy I was able to even be here today and be able to do this."

It's a display of the tenacity and ambition that's defined Starr's career to date.

Discovered singing covers on YouTube at the age of 18, she became the first African woman to win best international act at the Mobo Awards, and the first Nigerian woman to surpass one billion video views on YouTube.

In 2024, she was the first Afrobeats artist to play Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage – and finished her set by declaring she'd return as a headliner. Last year, she modelled for Di Petsa at London Fashion Week, closing their show in a white lace two-piece, flanked by an angel.

So it's hardly a surprise that Starr pitches up to our interview with a sort of celestial confidence. She's given to grand proclamations like "I'm unstoppable", or "I will exist in multitudes". But somehow, she never sounds arrogant or conceited.

That's probably due to a sense of humour so dry it could soak up a tsunami. Starr is criminally sarcastic, and delights in winding people up.

For example: When music legend Stevie Wonder phoned to congratulate Starr on a Grammy nomination, she goaded him into a playful argument about zodiac signs.

"I was trying to one-up him every single time, and he was trying to one-up me. It was almost like a battle," she recalls.

Starr eventually got to the point where she told Wonder, a Taurus, that "Tauruses ain't crap".

"I'm sure he was like, 'Who is this? What do you want from me?' But it was a very cute conversation. I respect it."

It's an unorthodox approach to making friends, but it seems to work.

Over the course of her career, Starr's hooked up with Coldplay, Tyla, David Guetta, Le Sserafim and Kelly Rowland from Destiny's Child.

Her new album boasts collaborations with Afrobeats legends Wizkid and Rema, as well as One Direction's Zayn Malik and rising R&B singer KWN.

The album is her first under a new management deal with Jay-Z's Roc Nation, and a relocation to New York. Leaving Lagos was a big upheaval, she confessed in an essay posted to her Substack last year.

"New York is basically a walk-in freezer with rent," she wrote. "It's so cold it feels like the city is actively trying to unalive my motivation… I'm not scared, I promise."

Behind the move was a desire to explore new influences and expand her sound. So you get a track like Where Do We Go, which marries a sashaying Afrobeats rhythm to a hypnotic electronic pulse.

"Like, the rebel I am, I love to juxtapose," she says.

"I don't like being normal and boring. So the idea of writing a heartbreak song on a beat like that, where you can dance to it, was just very enticing. I love things like that."

The lyrics were inspired by a secretive relationship "that was stuck in a rut but I kept coming back to it".

We've all been there. It's all too easy to settle for an imperfect partner because they're a comfortable and familiar presence.

Starr admits the thought of starting over with someone else filled her with fear.

"You're back to square one, and somebody's asking for your favourite colour again.

"I'm like, 'Oh my God! Can we, like, not do that?'"

The problem with staying in the relationship, however, was the way it affected the rest of her life.

"You keep accepting things lower than your standard, and that influences every single thing in your life - because when you let yourself go, romantically and emotionally, it affects you physically, and the music, and all of that.

"So even though I enjoyed [the romance] while it lasted, I picked my priorities and what was most important to me. And that relationship wasn't as important as the music... or anything else."

The story could act as a metaphor for the entire album. After the runaway success of her breakout single, Rush, and her second album, The Year I Turned 21, Starr was beginning to feel trapped by other people's expectations.

"Just like any other pop artist, passive listeners get attached to the songs they know - the popular songs.

"Then you're stuck between creating for the passive listeners and creating for your core fans who want you to do more.

"So that can limit you, because you stop thinking as an artist and start thinking about making music just for consumers.

"But I'm not meant to conform. It's just not who I am. I will rebel against every single preconception and every stereotype."

So she's ditched the teenage angst of her debut, but also the poise of its follow-up. This is an album about walking to her own rhythm, as Starr grows into autonomy and womanhood.

On Misunderstood, she laughs at the people who told her she'd "never make it on her own"; while the laid back groove of Treasure allows Starr to pause and savour her success.

" Give me some fun / Pure enjoyment / Take a photo of me ," she sings in Yoruba.

The most infectious song on the album is Ms Paper, which takes a detour into Bouyon – a Dominican music characterised by high tempos and frantic percussion. It was recorded almost by accident at the end of a session with French-Congolese star Theodora on a hot and sticky February night in LA.

They'd actually finished working for the day, and had just polished off a boozy dinner of Congolese food when inspiration struck.

"The AC in the studio wasn't working, so everybody's delirious, everybody's sweating, everybody's drunk," Starr says.

"At one point we're probably taking off tops. I changed outfit twice because I was drenched in sweat."

It sounds like a recipe for disaster, but when you play it back, you can practically see the steam rising from your speakers.

Live snippets of the song have already gone viral, suggesting Starr has another hefty hit on her hands. At the same time, she's faced criticism in Nigeria from people who feel she's diluting her musical heritage by chasing a more global sound

"People have a certain template they think I should follow, and it's like, you cannot tell me how to dream," she says.

"I'm able to honour my culture, but also try new things, because that's who I am."

Starr answers her critics, in a roundabout way, on her album cover - where she pairs a club-ready gold dress with a traditional gele headwrap.

"I wanted young girls in Kwara State or Erin-Ile to see this and feel represented," she told Capital Xtra .

"I'm not the first to do it, I won't be the last to do it - but I want people to feel confident in their culture and wear [the gele] like the crown that it is."

Not for the first time, her instincts proved right. Starr's stunning, retro-futuristic look has gone viral, inspiring dozens of copycats, and tempering at least some of the criticism of her new direction.

As she says in her new song, Amazing: " If they're gonna talk, I'll give them something to talk about ".

"That's definitely my mantra," she says.

"And do you know what? I think I need to listen to myself more because I have all the answers in my music."

articles.title: O que realmente acontece com seus dados quando você clica em 'deletar'? | G1
articles.standfirst: Um equívoco comum é achar que deletar equivale a apagar totalmente os dados, mas esta visão está, em grande parte, errada.
articles.summary: Um equívoco comum é achar que deletar equivale a apagar totalmente os dados, mas esta visão está, em grande parte, errada.
articles.body:
"Deletar" é algo comum na vida moderna. Estamos sempre enviando arquivos e pastas para a lixeira de nossos aparelhos e, muitas vezes, nos livramos de contas pessoais indesejadas. Mas você sabe o que realmente acontece quando você clica no botão "deletar"?

O processo de exclusão costuma ser mal explicado pelos provedores de tecnologia. A falta de transparência sobre como as solicitações são processadas e a ausência de uma confirmação clara de que os dados foram removidos são frequentemente destacadas em pesquisas.

Essas questões não se limitam aos sistemas operacionais. Em plataformas de mídia social e em uma ampla gama de serviços por assinatura, os mecanismos de exclusão costumam ser igualmente pouco claros. Tais equívocos podem ter sérias implicações para o bem-estar dos usuários, expondo-os a vulnerabilidades de segurança e problemas de privacidade.

Uma complicação adicional é que muitos usuários temem perder dados, arquivos, fotos e vídeos por meio de exclusão acidental – uma condição apelidada de "diagrafofobia" .

Um equívoco comum é achar que "deletar" significa "apagar", mas, em grande parte, a ideia está errada — Foto: Bruno Saito/Pexels

O que acontece com seus dados na internet quando você morre?

Embora não se trate de uma patologia reconhecida, estudos sobre o comportamento de acumulação digital mostram que algumas pessoas ficam muito ansiosas com a ideia de perder ou excluir acidentalmente informações pessoais, como fotos e músicas .

Essas preocupações aumentam a quantidade de dados pessoais que não são acessados, mas também não são excluídos, ficando expostos a um possível uso indevido.

Um equívoco comum é achar que "deletar" significa "apagar" – a ideia de que, uma vez que um item excluído não esteja mais visível, ele tenha sido completamente apagado, sem possibilidade de recuperação. Isso está, em grande parte, errado.

Quando os usuários deletam arquivos – movendo-os para a lixeira e, em seguida, excluindo-os permanentemente –, os dados não são, na verdade, apagados.

Em vez disso, o sistema marca o espaço de armazenamento como reutilizável e atualiza os metadados para desvincular o arquivo.

Mas o conteúdo subjacente muitas vezes permanece recuperável com as ferramentas certas, especialmente quando os dados estão duplicados em vários sistemas ou dispositivos.

Como excluir conta no Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, X e TikTok

Muitos usuários temem perder dados, arquivos, fotos e vídeos por meio de exclusão acidental — Foto: Ujesh Krishnan/Unsplash

Formas mais robustas de exclusão incluem a destruição física do meio de armazenamento, a sobrescrita dos blocos de memória com novos dados para ocultar o original, ou a criptografia dos dados seguida da destruição da chave.

Tais métodos, no entanto, podem ser caros ou tornar o dispositivo de armazenamento inutilizável (por exemplo, ao sobrescrever dados em mídias magnéticas). As características da infraestrutura em nuvem também representam desafios para a exclusão segura de dados.

Da mesma forma, o conteúdo em redes sociais públicas pode não ser realmente apagado após a exclusão devido a respostas, comentários e arquivos da internet, que podem armazenar as postagens de alguma forma. O significado de um tuíte excluído pode, por exemplo, ser recriado com base em respostas e menções.

Outro equívoco é achar que excluir um aplicativo de um dispositivo apaga automaticamente a conta associada . Os usuários frequentemente deixam contas de aplicativos móveis sem excluir porque não sabem de sua existência, já que excluíram o aplicativo relacionado.

São as chamadas contas "zumbis" – perfis abandonados em uma ampla variedade de serviços, desde aplicativos de compras e armazenamento até namoro, finanças e streaming.

Milhões de usuários têm contas zumbis, com dados pessoais que estão vulneráveis a ataques cibernéticos e violações de dados.

O crescimento exponencial da IA levanta uma outra questão: os dados podem realmente ser excluídos depois de terem sido usados para treinar modelos de IA? Os módulos de aprendizado de máquina memorizam facilmente os dados com os quais foram treinados, mas "desaprender" é difícil.

Em teoria, pessoas na Europa e em muitos outros países ao redor do mundo têm um "direito de ser esquecido" previsto em lei . Isso significa que podem solicitar o apagamento total de quaisquer dados pessoais que uma plataforma ou empresa possa ter.

Os desenvolvedores de IA são considerados controladores de dados de acordo com as leis do Regulamento Geral de Proteção de Dados (RGPD) da UE, por exemplo, e estão sujeitos a essa obrigação.

Mas não há diretrizes claras sobre como a exclusão deve ser aplicada nos sistemas de IA. Os órgãos reguladores podem solicitar a exclusão, mas as empresas de IA podem argumentar que a conformidade é inviável devido a restrições técnicas.

ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude, Mistral AI, Gemini, Copilot e Poe — Foto: Solen Feyissa/Unsplash

Para combater os riscos decorrentes da exclusão incompleta, acredito que haja uma necessidade urgente de fornecer informações concisas, acessíveis e claras sobre como a exclusão realmente funciona.

Uma abordagem possível é a "exclusão explicável" – um protocolo desenvolvido por Marvin Ramokapane no Centro Nacional de Pesquisa sobre Privacidade, Redução de Danos e Influência Adversária Online (Rephrain), sediado na Universidade de Bristol, Reino Unido.

A intenção é tornar os processos de exclusão mais transparentes e compreensíveis, sem sobrecarregar o usuário com informações excessivas de uma só vez.

A exclusão explicável divide as informações em seis categorias: o quê, como, quando, quem, onde e por quê (veja o diagrama). Cada uma oferece ao usuário informações sucintas sobre essa parte do processo.

A exclusão explicável foi projetada para dar aos usuários controle sobre suas ações, autonomia para escolher o tipo de exclusão mais adequado para eles e a garantia de que as ações desejadas foram realizadas. Ela também pode amenizar a ansiedade de perder dados acidentalmente, oferecendo opções para recuperação.

Embora a exclusão explicável ainda não tenha sido adotada na prática, os provedores de serviços — tanto plataformas quanto desenvolvedores — poderiam aumentar a confiança dos usuários ao adotar tais protocolos. Essa estrutura também pode servir como prova de conformidade com as normas do GDPR da UE e com o direito ao esquecimento.

A maioria de nós usa sistemas que coletam e armazenam nossos dados diariamente. Se esses sistemas explicassem claramente o que armazenam e o que a exclusão realmente significa, isso poderia nos ajudar a identificar as contas e os dados que representam um risco real — e a retomar o controle de nossas pegadas digitais.

Dana Lungu não presta consultoria, trabalha, possui ações ou recebe financiamento de qualquer empresa ou organização que poderia se beneficiar com a publicação deste artigo e não revelou nenhum vínculo relevante além de seu cargo acadêmico.

articles.title: Instagram ganha nova identidade visual após 10 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Ícone de câmera foi mantido, mas plataforma ganhou nova tipografia e mudanças nas cores, animações e elementos gráficos. Última grande reformulação havia ocorrido em 2016.
articles.summary: Ícone de câmera foi mantido, mas plataforma ganhou nova tipografia e mudanças nas cores, animações e elementos gráficos. Última grande reformulação havia ocorrido em 2016.
articles.body:
Instagram muda sua identidade visual pela primeira vez em 10 anos — Foto: Divulgação/Instagram

O Instagram anunciou nesta quinta-feira (13) uma renovação de sua identidade visual, que inclui uma nova tipografia, ajustes nas cores, movimentos e outros elementos gráficos. A mudança foi anunciada por Adam Mosseri, diretor do Instagram.

Essa é a primeira grande atualização da identidade visual da plataforma em 10 anos. A última grande mudança ocorreu em 2016, quando o aplicativo abandonou o visual retrô e adotou a identidade colorida e minimalista.

A nova fonte moderniza a caligrafia do Instagram. — Foto: Divulgação/Instagram

Em publicação oficial, o Instagram afirmou que está “escrevendo um novo capítulo” da plataforma, com uma logotipia renovada e um sistema de marca inspirado no “espírito artesanal” de suas raízes criativas.

🗒️Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Mande para o g1

“Ele [o novo sistema de arte] foi criado para inspirar ações corajosas e dar às pessoas a confiança para criar e se expressar como realmente são, de forma livre e plena”, disse May Hartono, diretora de design de marca da Meta.

"Estamos escrevendo um novo capítulo no Instagram com uma logotipia renovada e um sistema de marca que reflete o espírito artesanal das nossas raízes criativas. Esse trabalho se estendeu a todo o sistema da marca — abrangendo tipografia, movimento, cores e muito mais —, tudo concebido para destacar a criatividade infinita da nossa comunidade", explicou a empresa no post oficial da mudança.

Logotipo e ícone: o tradicional símbolo de câmera continua como principal referência, mas ganhou uma construção visual atualizada;

Tipografia: a marca passou a utilizar uma nova linguagem tipográfica própria;

Cores: a paleta foi ajustada para mudar a identidade;

Movimento e animações: a nova identidade incorpora uma linguagem própria para elementos animados;

Elementos gráficos: o sistema visual foi desenvolvido para se adaptar a diferentes formatos e experiências dentro da plataforma.

Na prática, a nova proposta deixa de lado parte dos elementos mais ornamentados da identidade anterior e aposta em uma linguagem mais contemporânea e limpa.

Segundo a plataforma, a renovação busca recuperar o caráter criativo e artesanal de suas origens e, ao mesmo tempo, criar uma identidade capaz de acompanhar a evolução do aplicativo.

Desde o lançamento, em 6 de outubro de 2010, o Instagram passou por diferentes transformações visuais.

A plataforma foi criada pelo norte-americano Kevin Systrom e pelo engenheiro de software brasileiro Mike Krieger. No início, o aplicativo tinha uma estética inspirada em câmeras fotográficas antigas, com o famoso ícone de câmera retrô.

A mudança mais marcante aconteceu em 2016, quando o Instagram adotou o gradiente colorido e o desenho minimalista que se tornaram sua identidade durante a última década.
